EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  July 19, 2016

CALL TO ORDER

CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:02 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Bill Kemp
Pam Schachter
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT – EXCUSED

Susan Brtis
Lisa Hawkins

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT – UNEXCUSED
Carol Dean-Porter
Patricia Harik
Victor Yoo

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT

Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 23, 2016

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SCHACHTER

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE MAY 23, 2016 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JULY 19, 2016  1
 AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None.

HOWLETT PARK EQUESTRIAN STRUCTURES SPECIFICATIONS UPDATE

The Community Services Director indicated that the City was receiving guidance from Allen
Prefab Building Corporation in Gardena in revising the new horse show office, horse show
judges booth, and dressage show judges booth bid specifications. The Howlett Park Equestrian
Structures Subcommittee had recently revised the specifications and are awaiting further
feedback from this firm. MEMBER SCHACHTER noted that the City was fortunate to have this
company available to assist in developing each structure to provide better functionality than the
current structures in Howlett Park’s equestrian center.

POTENTIAL PVPHA TRAIL OBSTACLES DONATION
The Community Services Director reviewed the staff report noting that the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Horsemens Association (PVPHA) had obtained used trail obstacles equipment and
that City staff had confirmed that they were in reasonable condition. He indicated that if the City
accepts the donated equipment, that it should not be with a condition that the trail obstacles be
required to be maintained or replaced in perpetuity.

PVPHA Board Member, Melody Colbert, 4604 Rockbluff Drive, addressed the Equestrian
Committee stating that there continues to be new horsemanship disciplines being developed.
She noted the PVPHA Board of Directors would soon be voting as to whether to donate them
to the City for potential use in the lower lunging arena in Ernie Howlett Park. It was her
observation that this arena had low usage and that the light trail obstacles (made from PVC
pipe) could be easily removed when requested when horse shows needed this arena.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  THAT IF THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA HORSEMENS ASSOCIATION VOTES TO
  DONATE THE TRAIL OBSTACLES TO THE CITY TO MAKE A RECOMMENDATION
  TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION TO ACCEPT THE EQUIPMENT
  DONATION FOR PLACEMENT IN ERNIE HOWLETT PARK’S LOWER LUNGING
  ARENA.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

CITY CELEBRATION EQUESTRIAN ACTIVITIES UPDATE

MEMBER SCHACHTER reviewed the list of demonstrations, horsemanship events, clinics,
sponsors, and booths planned for this year’s new venue. CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ praised

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JULY 19, 2016  2
 MEMBER SCHACHTER for the amount of planning and coordination time she had committed
to this event.

PROPOSED NEW ARENA IN CHANDLER PARK

The Community Services Director provided an overview of the steps that had been taken in
2005 when a proposed new dressage arena had been considered for installation in Chandler

Park by the Equestrian Committee and the Park and Activities Commission. Unfortunately, a
survey of the adjacent Roanwood and Ranchview Homeowners Associations did not support
installation of the proposed arena. He indicated that the Park and Activities Commission would
likely utilize a similar method to verify community support should the Equestrian Committee
again recommend consideration of the addition of a horse arena in Chandler Park.

MEMBER SHINN restated her concerns that the nearby Peter Weber Equestrian Center, which
has increased its boarding capacity, was causing increased use of the Chandler Park arena
and causing potential safety concerns. She further noted that the renovated round pen in
Pepperwood Park has not alleviated the crowded conditions in Chandler Park’s arena.

MEMBER SHINN stated that a Dressage Arena should be considered for construction in
Chandler Park. MEMBER SILVANO stated her belief that it should be a public arena and not
for exclusive use by the Peter Weber Equestrian Center in order to ease the overcrowding in
the Chandler Park arena. The Community Services Director concurred with MEMBER SHINN
that measures such as landscaping to screen the proposed arena, installation of low dust
footing material, instituting a daily arena watering schedule, and prohibiting night usage,
lighting, and amplified sound in this arena would ease any concerns from the adjacent
neighborhood. He noted that the proposed arena was still under consideration by Los Angeles
County Fourth District Supervisor Knabe.

Audience member, Rich Oldroyd, 40 Ranchview Road, stated that he opposed the addition of
an arena in Chandler Park in 2005 and continues to oppose its construction. He believes that
the City needs to keep its current green space for the residents in this area of the City.

Audience member, Sheryl Steckel, 3 Strawberry Lane, recommended installing higher fencing
in the proposed dressage arena on the Palos Verdes Landfill to make it a multi-purpose arena.
MEMBER SCHACHTER disagreed, indicating that it’s hard to mix dressage riding with other
horse riding disciplines. MEMBER SHINN believes that 3-rail fencing could be installed around
the proposed dressage arena to keep horses within this site should they jump out of the lower
fenced dressage arena. She also noted that it’s common for dog owners to allow their dogs off
leash on the Palos Verdes Landfill and the outer fencing would keep dogs from getting too close
and startling horses in the arena.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JULY 19, 2016  3
 MEMBER KEMP moved, seconded by MEMBER SCHACHTER

  FOR THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE TO NOT CONTINUE CONSIDERATION OF AN
  ADDITIONAL HORSE ARENA IN CHANDLER PARK AT THIS TIME.

AYES: Kemp, Schachter, Schmitz, Silvano
NOES: Shinn
ABSENT: Susan Brtis, Carol Dean-Porter, Patricia Harik, Lisa Hawkins, Victor Yoo

CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ STATED THAT THE MOTION CARRIED.

CHANDLER AND HOWLETT PARK WATERING

MEMBER SHINN stated that horse trainers and riders routinely do not water the public arena
causing large dust clouds to rise around the arenas. Following discussion by the Committee,
it was recommend that staff consider installing an automatic watering system also on Howlett
Park’s arenas and to water all of the public arenas at approximately 6:30 a.m. each morning. It
was also recommended that another Horse Trainers meeting be scheduled to remind them
about watering and that the City’s Zoning and Code Enforcement Administrator conduct spot
checks of arena users to verify they are turning on the sprinklers. CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ
requested that a letter reminding Horse Trainers to water the arenas be mailed out. MEMBER
SHINN also noted that the Howlett Park equestrian center’s sprinklers do not reach the middle
of the two large arenas.

Audience member, Sheryl Steckel, 3 Strawberry Lane, recommended that Dapplegray Park
should have the automatic watering system come on throughout the day with a beeper
forewarning riders and Horse Trainers that the arena will be sprinkled within a few minutes.

Audience member, Becky Martin, 2301 243rd Street, Torrance, stated that the GGT footing in
Howlett Park arena #1 can take a large amount of watering and finds that it helps to water this
arena the night before the Los Serranos Horse Shows.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE
EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG.

ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
Audience member, Sheryl Steckel, 3 Strawberry Lane, reported that branches should be cut
back on the Palos Verdes Drive North, Botanical Gardens, and Rolling Hills Road bridle trails.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JULY 19, 2016  4
 MEMBER KEMP requested an update on the installation timelines for the horse riders and
pedestrians lighted crossings on Rolling Hills Road and Palos Verdes Drive North.

MEMBER SCHACHTER reported that the Howlett Park arenas do not have the most current
arena regulations posted.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ reported that the Future Agenda Items listed will now include an
estimated timeline as to when they may be placed on a future Equestrian Committee agenda.

A.  POTENTIAL NEW DRESSAGE ARENA ON PV LANDFIL (Fall 2016 – Per Supervisor
  Knabe’s approval)

B.  NEW PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM BUILDING (Fall 2016 –
  After PWEC Grant Reimbursements Received)

C.  POTENTIAL PWEC HORSE TRAILER PARKING AT RECYCLE CENTER (Fall 2016 -
  Per Supervisor Knabe’s approval)

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:00 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
